body.statement: Under the observed-law conditions and source-compatible parallel trends on the baseline-treatment support \(X_0\), the continuous-trend compatible-completion subclass \(\mathfrak Q(P)\) is nonempty if and only if \(\mathcal C_P\neq\varnothing\). Whenever these sets are nonempty, \(\{\theta(Q):Q\in\mathfrak Q(P)\}=\Theta(P)\). For every \(u\in\mathcal C_P\), the affine one-argument static-schedule lift produces \(Q_u\in\mathfrak Q(P)\), preserves the entire joint law \(P\), satisfies \(m_{Q_u}=u\in C(X_0)\), and makes both period schedules individually \(K\)-Lipschitz. Moreover, \(Y_2^{Q_u}(d)-Y_1^{Q_u}(d)=\Delta Y-g(X,Z)+u(X)\) for every \(d\in I\), so the constructed witness satisfies the stronger all-\(I\) parallel-trends equality even though the maintained source condition is required only on \(X_0\), and \(\theta(Q_u)=(T-J_P(u))/A\). This is a strict partial-identification extension of the 2024 proceedings Theorem 1 weighted WAOSS formula: it remains sharp when baseline-conditional quasi-stayer support fails and specializes to that singleton formula under the stronger baseline-conditional support regime. No equality with a broader discontinuous-trend completion class is asserted.
body.justification: This is the causal kernel: it replaces an unsupported conditional limit by a two-sided, full-observed-law sharp characterization.
body.gap: Assumption 4 of de Chaisemartin, D'Haultf\oe{}uille, and Vazquez-Bare (2024) imposes only \(P(|\Delta D|\le\eta)>0\), while the Appendix proof of Theorem 1 invokes \(P(|\Delta D|\le\eta\mid D_1)>0\) immediately before display (4). Under the source's parallel-trends condition on the baseline-treatment support, the present theorem repairs the marginal-support claim with a sharp full-law set. Assumption 5 of de Chaisemartin et al. (arXiv:2201.06898v1, Section 4.1) supplies an analogous baseline-conditional support regime, but its Theorem 3 identifies the unweighted switcher-slope target \(\delta_1\), not WAOSS.
body.consumer: Applied continuous-dose DiD analyses with changing temperatures can report a robustness set without imposing a parametric extrapolation across baseline-specific support holes.
body.proof_tex:
Because \(I\) is compact, \(|Z|\leq \operatorname{diam}(I)\) almost surely.  The no-stayer condition gives \(|Z|>0\) almost surely, and hence
\[
0<A=E_P|Z|\leq \operatorname{diam}(I)<\infty.
\]
Observed integrability also gives \(E_P|\Delta Y|<\infty\), so \(T\) is finite.

First take \(Q\in\mathfrak Q(P)\), and write \(m=m_Q\).  Consistency gives the pointwise decomposition
\[
\Delta Y
=Y_2^Q(D_2)-Y_1^Q(D_1)
=\{Y_2^Q(D_2)-Y_2^Q(D_1)\}
 +\{Y_2^Q(D_1)-Y_1^Q(D_1)\}.
\]
The jointly measurable version in conditional parallel trends may be evaluated at \(D_1=X\); therefore
\[
E_Q[Y_2^Q(D_1)-Y_1^Q(D_1)\mid X,Z]=m(X).
\]
The observed-law match then implies, for \(P_{XZ}\)-almost every \((x,z)\),
\[
g(x,z)-m(x)
=E_Q[Y_2^Q(D_2)-Y_2^Q(D_1)\mid X=x,Z=z].
\]
The mean-movement bound yields
\[
|g(x,z)-m(x)|\leq K|z|\qquad P_{XZ}\text{-almost everywhere}.
\]
Both sides define continuous functions on \(H\): continuity of \(g\) is assumed and continuity of \(m\) is part of the legal-completion definition.  If the displayed inequality failed at a point of \(H=\operatorname{supp}_P(X,Z)\), it would fail on a relatively open neighborhood of that point; every such neighborhood has positive \(P_{XZ}\)-probability, a contradiction.  Thus it holds everywhere on \(H\).  The trend bound and trend Lipschitz condition now show \(m\in\mathcal C_P\).  This proves
\[
\mathfrak Q(P)\neq\varnothing\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\mathcal C_P\neq\varnothing.
\]

The same decomposition identifies the value associated with any legal completion.  By iterated expectations and the definition of \(\nu_P\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
A\theta(Q)
&=E_Q\!\left[S\{Y_2^Q(D_2)-Y_2^Q(D_1)\}\right]\\
&=E_P[S\Delta Y]-E_Q\!\left[S\{Y_2^Q(D_1)-Y_1^Q(D_1)\}\right]\\
&=T-E_P[S m(X)]
=T-\int_{X_0}m(x)\,d\nu_P(x)
=T-J_P(m).
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently every legal value belongs to \(\Theta(P)\).

Conversely, fix \(u\in\mathcal C_P\) and retain the observed vector with law \(P\).  Since \(P(Z=0)=0\), define
\[
b_u=\frac{g(X,Z)-u(X)}{Z}
\]
off the null event \(\{Z=0\}\), and set it equal to zero on that event.  The support inequality in the definition of \(\mathcal C_P\) gives \(|b_u|\leq K\) almost surely.  Define, simultaneously for every \(d\in I\),
\[
Y_1^{Q_u}(d)=Y_1+b_u(d-D_1),
\qquad
Y_2^{Q_u}(d)=Y_2+b_u(d-D_2).
\]
These schedules are jointly measurable.  They satisfy consistency pointwise:
\[
Y_1^{Q_u}(D_1)=Y_1,
\qquad
Y_2^{Q_u}(D_2)=Y_2.
\]
Thus the complete joint observed law, not merely its moments, remains \(P\).  For fixed \(d\in I\), compactness of \(I\) and \(|b_u|\leq K\) give
\[
|Y_t^{Q_u}(d)|\leq |Y_t|+K\operatorname{diam}(I),
\]
so latent integrability follows from observed integrability.  Both schedules are individually \(K\)-Lipschitz because
\[
|Y_t^{Q_u}(d)-Y_t^{Q_u}(d')|=|b_u|\,|d-d'|\leq K|d-d'|.
\]
Their period difference is independent of \(d\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
Y_2^{Q_u}(d)-Y_1^{Q_u}(d)
&=\Delta Y+b_u(D_1-D_2)\\
&=\Delta Y-b_uZ
=\Delta Y-g(X,Z)+u(X).
\end{aligned}
\]
Since \(g(X,Z)=E_P[\Delta Y\mid X,Z]\),
\[
E_{Q_u}[Y_2^{Q_u}(d)-Y_1^{Q_u}(d)\mid X,Z]=u(X)
=E_{Q_u}[Y_2^{Q_u}(d)-Y_1^{Q_u}(d)\mid X]
\]
for every \(d\in I\).  This proves the stronger all-\(I\) parallel-trends equality, and setting \(d=X\) gives \(m_{Q_u}=u\).  The remaining shape restrictions on \(m_{Q_u}\) follow directly from \(u\in\mathcal C_P\).  Moreover,
\[
Y_2^{Q_u}(D_2)-Y_2^{Q_u}(D_1)=b_uZ=g(X,Z)-u(X),
\]
whose absolute conditional mean is at most \(K|Z|\).  Hence \(Q_u\in\mathfrak Q(P)\), proving the reverse nonemptiness implication.  Finally,
\[
\theta(Q_u)
=\frac{E_P[S\{g(X,Z)-u(X)\}]}{A}
=\frac{T-J_P(u)}{A},
\]
where \(E_P[Sg(X,Z)]=E_P[S\Delta Y]=T\) by iterated expectations.  Thus every point of \(\Theta(P)\) is attained by a legal full-data law, while the first part proved that no other value is legal.  This establishes the asserted full-observed-law sharp equality on the declared continuous-trend completion class; the construction itself also establishes the claimed individual schedule regularity.
